newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money slips to 3.05 pct after Buba add.
newsitem.headline: German call money slips to 3.05 pct after Buba add.

text.p: German call money rates dipped slightly on Wednesday as the Bundesbank helped ease liquidity conditions by injecting an additional 1.7 billion marks into the system at the weekly tender award.
Dealers said the bulk of trades was conducted between 3.08/10 percent with rates slipping as slow as 3.05 percent. This compares with Tuesday's rates of 3.10/15 percent.

But dealers were also not certain where the market would head in coming days, saying that the Bundesbank's injection of funds was small enough to signal that rates should continue to trade broadly in a range.
The Bundesbank this morning added a net 1.7 billion marks to the market at a fixed rate of three percent, the rate that has prevailed since August.

Banks held 38.3 billion marks in non-interest bearing accounts at the Bundesbank on Tuesday, up from Monday's 37.4 billion marks held. The monthly average however slipped to 39.6 billion marks compared with 39.8 billion marks on Monday.

Lombard borrowings rose to 100 million marks on Tuesday after being negligible on Monday. The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 3.12333 percent on Wednesday compared with 3.14533 percent on Tuesday.
